new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type part-of-speech-conditioned word stress: in nouns and adjectives primary stress falls on the final syllable of the word; in verbs it tends to the initial syllable, specifically the preverb/prefix (ba-, da-, de-, ha-, hā-) in prefixed verb forms (confirmed independently by Mokhtarian 2005: 15, 'Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich'). No secondary stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly denied: 'Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress' (p. 171).
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: stress on the preverb/initial syllable rather than final (pp. 164, 171, 178). Mokhtarian 2005 (Tübingen dissertation, pp. 10-17) adds that plural -(h)ā/-un, definite-object -e, attributive -e and indirect-object -ra are unstressed (so stress stays on the stem-final syllable), while substantivizing -i and the infinitive ending -(j)en are stressed and preterite prefixes attract the word accent. The p. 164 statement is hedged with 'generally' and is a comparison with Persian, not an exhaustive rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('at the word level'); citation/elicited forms from native speakers of the Amol, Babol and Reineh dialects. The article's topic is vowel dissimilation, so the stress statement is brief background, not a dedicated prosodic analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Mahdavi Mazdeh & Nehzati 2024 describe the dialects of Amol, Babol and Reineh (Larijan, south of Amol) in central Mazandaran, all within Glottolog's single language maza1291; Mokhtarian 2005 sketches 'the present-day Mazandarani dialect' without naming a locality. The earlier scan's named sources (Yoshie 1996, Nawata 1984) concern the Sari dialect, also maza1291. Glottolog's other refs Borjian 2012 (Velātru/Gachsar) and 2013 (Yushij) describe Caspian-Persian transition-zone varieties in the Alborz, not the core language.

new_statements.quote: [S. 10-11, §3.1] Der Plural wird regelhaft mit den Suffixen -(h)ā und -un gebildet, welche dem Nomen angefügt werden und nicht die Betonung auf sich ziehen. [S. 11, §3.2] Das bestimmte direkte Objekt erhält ein Suffix /-e/, welches nicht die Betonung auf sich zieht [...] Das indirekte Objekt wird mit dem unbetonten Suffix /-ra/ gebildet [S. 15, §6.4] Das Präteritum wird meist durch die Präfixe /ba-/, /da-/, /de-/, /ha-/ und /hā-/ + Präteritalstamm + Personalendung gebildet. Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich. [S. 17, §6.4.7] Infinitiv wird aus dem Präterialstamm und der betonten Endung /-(j)en/, gebildet: /da-ket-en/ „fallen“
new_statements.translation: [pp. 10-11, §3.1] The plural is formed regularly with the suffixes -(h)ā and -un, which are attached to the noun and do not attract the stress. [p. 11, §3.2] The definite direct object receives a suffix /-e/, which does not attract the stress [...] The indirect object is formed with the unstressed suffix /-ra/. [p. 15, §6.4] The preterite is mostly formed with the prefixes /ba-/, /da-/, /de-/, /ha-/ and /hā-/ + preterite stem + personal ending. The prefix here attracts the word accent. [p. 17, §6.4.7] The infinitive is formed from the preterite stem and the stressed ending /-(j)en/: /da-ket-en/ 'to fall'

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing statement (Mahdavi Mazdeh & Nehzati 2024: stress final in nouns/adjectives, on the preverb/first syllable in prefixed verbs, no secondary stress) and adds morpheme-level detail: which nominal suffixes are unstressed (plural, object, attributive), which suffixes are stressed (nominalizing -i, infinitive -(j)en, subjunctive endings), and that the preterite prefix bears the word accent. It never states a general rule, so it cannot independently confirm 'final' for underived nouns. The catalog record itself has an empty rule field; this work does not fill it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The sketch states no general placement rule and has no stress/accent section; stress is mentioned only as a property of individual morphemes. Taken together: nominal inflectional suffixes (plural -(h)ā/-un, definite-object -e, attributive -e, indirect-object -ra) are unstressed, so stress stays on the stem; derivational nominalizing -i (p. 14: 'Durch das betonte Suffixmorphem /-i/ erfolgt die Substantivierung der Adjektive') and the infinitive ending -(j)en are stressed (final); in finite preterite (and imperative/subjunctive-type prefixed) verbs the prefix ba-/da-/de-/ha-/hā- carries the word accent (initial). The 'fixed: final syllable' label is my inference from these morpheme statements, not a rule the author states; confidence low.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbal prefixes take the word accent in the preterite (p. 15); the infinitive ending -(j)en is stressed even in prefixed infinitives (da-ket-én, ba-merd-én, p. 17); p. 22-23 (PDF 25-26), in the medieval-Tabari section: 'Aufgrund der Fehlens diakritischer Vokalzeichen, lässt sich in der HS nicht zwischen Indikativ- und Konjunktivendungen unterscheiden. In Māz sind diese Affixe betont.' (in modern Mazandarani the subjunctive personal endings are stressed). Also p. 10 §2.1: vowels /i, e, o, u/ are long in monosyllables and in the stressed syllable of polysyllables (stress conditions vowel length).
new_statements.identity_note: The dissertation's main body is a philological edition of a medieval Tabari (Old Mazandarani) translation of al-Harīrī's Maqāmāt (ms. Malek 2487); the stress remarks quoted come from the prefatory 'Kurze Beschreibung der heutigen māzandarānischen Mundart' (pp. 7-17), which describes the modern spoken Mazandarani dialect without naming a specific locality in the pages read. The remark on pp. 22-23 contrasts the manuscript's Tabari with modern 'Māz'. The Glottolog open_url (w210.ub.uni-tuebingen.de) no longer resolves (automated download rc 6); the same PDF (1,014,409 bytes) is served at https://publikationen.uni-tuebingen.de/xmlui/bitstream/handle/10900/46247/pdf/Maqamat_i_Hariri_%28tabarische_Mundart%29.pdf (HTTP 200 verified).
